evals.prompt: The accepted incident-triage workflow has one queue, a selected-incident detail drawer, and one primary action: Assign owner. The proposed visual brief adds a permanent activity column, a hero metric card, three nested bordered panels, and a bright animated background. Give the visual direction and implementation handoff.
evals.expected_output: Preserves the accepted workflow and makes the assignment action visually unmistakable; removes or defers nonessential visual layers; records a deliberate no; retains accessibility and necessary state visibility without a literal Steve Jobs imitation.
assertions: Names the user-facing benefit and keeps Assign owner as the visual focal action.
Removes or defers the permanent activity column, hero metric card, nested containers, or animated background unless evidence proves a primary-job need.
States a deliberate no instead of only saying the page should be minimal.
Preserves functional requirements, accessibility, and visible state treatment.
Returns visual-system constraints and an implementation handoff without reauthoring the interaction model.

farplane.title: Uses visual subtraction to protect a single operational focus

assertions: Names a visual concept drawn from the bakery or neighborhood world, not only adjectives such as clean, warm, or premium.
Presents three directions that differ in concept, not only in palette, font, or radius.
Chooses one direction against the scene sentence, focal action, or dials and gives a reason each other direction lost.
Keeps the reserve action and pickup code clear; the concept does not hurt the primary job.

Renders a key screen as a static HTML mock at a phone viewport with realistic content and reports its path and critique scores, or labels the critique `unrendered` with the reason; a text-only critique without that label fails.
Avoids banned AI tells such as purple-blue gradients, identical icon card grids, and gradient text.

Does not invent a new concept or run three new directions; names the existing concept or `none recorded`.
Fixes the hierarchy problem (overdue emphasis, row weight) with a small concrete change.

evals.prompt: New internal dispatch dashboard for a courier company: dispatchers watch about 40 live deliveries, spot late ones, and reassign drivers all shift long. No design system exists yet. Give the visual direction.
evals.expected_output: Treats this as product register for repeated work: names a concept from the courier world but keeps it quiet (accent, status color, icons, one signature moment) while layout stays dense and scannable; the three directions vary concept without turning the dashboard cinematic; dials stay in product or data-heavy ranges.
assertions: Classifies the surface as product or data-heavy register for repeated work.
Names a concept from the courier or dispatch world and limits it to accent, status color, icons, naming, or one signature moment rather than layout or decorative motion.
Keeps late deliveries and reassignment as the visual focus, scannable at about 40 rows.
Sets density at 6 or higher and motion at 4 or lower, or justifies any departure.

evals.prompt: Set the visual direction for the hero and first fold of a landing page that sells an AI engineering workflow setup to small dev teams. The operator says: "make it feel like the stuff I saved to the Tasty Pack this week, I love the empty space and the beige." The pack they mean is the attached fixture. Standing operator rules: never use orange, terracotta or rust anywhere; Farplane product dashboards keep zero-chroma concrete neutrals. No fonts or palette were stated beyond that. Give the visual brief and the implementation handoff.
evals.expected_output: Turns the saved references into a steal table with exact values, builds a three-role palette that works before its accent is added, translates the empty space into enforceable layout numbers, rejects the saved orange accents under the standing ban, and keeps the warm ground on the brand surface without leaking it into product dashboards.
assertions: Writes a steal table from the pack with exact hex values per trait and an adopt, adapt or reject call for each, instead of adjectives such as 'warm' or 'minimal'.

Assigns the palette by role (a ground or field, a figure or ink colour for type and main shapes, one accent) with an approximate share of the surface for each, and states that ground plus figure must work before the accent is added.
Reserves the single accent for the one focal action or mark (for example the primary CTA) rather than spreading it across the page.
Turns 'empty space' into checkable numbers, such as the share of the hero the subject or content may occupy, a maximum content width, or a margin scale, rather than only saying 'lots of whitespace'.
Rejects the saved tangerine and pumpkin accents because of the standing no-orange rule and names a non-orange substitute drawn from the pack.
Keeps the warm greige or oat ground to this brand surface and states that Farplane product dashboards stay on zero-chroma neutrals.
Does not copy the source's protected marks (Meta's #0866d8 blue as the brand colour, the Muse Wonder wordmark, or the film's people) and borrows the pattern instead.
